configs.description: The switch as it runs: the built-in AC supply and the blank cover over the FlexStack module slot. The C2960S-STACK module is optional (PDF p21, printed 1-19) and is not seated here.
configs.name: ac

configs.description: The same switch with the optional C2960S-STACK FlexStack module fitted in place of the blank cover (PDF p31, printed 1-7). Not a SKU: the stack kit is ordered separately (PDF p29, printed 1-5).
configs.name: with-flexstack-module

configs.description: WS-C2960S-48LPD-L, the model's only SKU (Table 1-1, LAN Base, PoE budget 370 W). It seats the blank cover in the FlexStack slot: the stack kit is a separate, optional part (PDF p21, printed 1-19) and the cover is removed only to fit the module (PDF p31).
configs.name: ws-c2960s-48lpd-l

gaps.wanted: The top, the bottom and the right wall. The guide's figures show the lid plain and no underside. Figure 1-12 (PDF p36, printed 1-12) shows the right wall only in part, behind the rack bracket. No held picture shows the part it hides. The right wall is left as a later part of its own.
The stretch of the left wall between 137 and 268 mm from the rear. The photographed switches are 299 mm deep. No held picture shows a 386 mm model's wall, so the stretch is drawn plain.

The RPS connector is the part cisco/rps2300-connector@2, drawn open where the photograph puts it. The part draws the plate, its two screw holes and the shroud with its dark top edge. It draws the housing and the two rows of eleven cavities, each with a contact and chamfered lower corners. It does not draw the slot in the screws, which the photograph shows at about one pixel. The rating strip stays chassis art. The line printed on the tab above the plate is not drawn; the printed legends are left to a later touch of their own. The photograph reads "+12V", a direct-current sign, "@11.25A", "-48V", a direct-current sign and "@7.8A". The mark after "11.25A" reads as a comma or a full stop; every other character is legible. The guide says the cover (two Phillips pan-head screws, Figure 1-15) goes on when no RPS is connected.

This model's own rear in colour. The only held rear in colour with the FlexStack slot is the NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-48LPD-L, whose plain plate reads #3f4447 and whose fitted module's plain frame reads #3f565d; the NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-24TS-L rear (no FlexStack slot, read for colour only) reads #404145. The drawn #404040 is within 7 levels of 255 of each. The guide's own drawing of the rear (Figure 1-10, PDF p19, printed 1-17) is pale grey (#d4d6d8) and shades one finish by the light on each face, so it conflicts with the photographs; the guide gives no housing colour. The rear is drawn charcoal, a stand-in that the owner may accept or replace. The front is not in doubt: the teal edge, charcoal panel and white console surround are what the four 2960-S stencils agree on, and Figure 1-1 draws the same scheme.

Cisco's logo is never drawn (the region `logo-zone` stays). The corner marks 1X, 11X, 2X, 12X and so on at the corners of each block read clearly on the stencil but sit where the jack part's box begins: each mark's inner 0.6 to 1.0 mm lies under the part, so a mark would be half hidden and is not drawn. The "POWER over ETHERNET" legend on the strip under the first block is drawn black as the 48FPD-L stencil prints it; the figure after it (a power in watts) is not legible there and is not drawn.

The ETSI mounting bracket, printed "700-19781XX" (PDF p34, printed 1-10). Its revision digits are not read, and the guide gives no contents or install steps beyond Figure 1-10, so no kit contract is written.

A square-on photograph or flat drawing of this model's own front. The only flat faces are community art of sibling models, and this model's own NetBox front is a different product, so every position is the 48FPD-L's.
The Mode button is drawn as plain panel art. No library part is a flush push button of this shape.

The RATING label beside the inlet is not drawn; the printed legends are left to a later touch of their own. The photograph prints "RATING", then "100-240V~", then "8-4A" and "50-60Hz" with a small mark between them. The small mark reads as a comma or a full stop; every other character is legible. The photograph is this model's rear by its name, but its figures differ from this model's row. Table 1-2 reads 5 to 2 A; the guide's drawing reads "12-6A".

A `common/led-arrow-sm` skin whose off fill is the stencil's solid light grey (#808080: 120 px, box (520,96,535,104) of a port arrow and 155 px, box (4660,118,4676,128) of the console arrow; each arrow 2.38 x 2.12 mm) without the dark fill and the #5b6167 edge. The part is on `main` and its skin is not edited, and a lamp's colour in the static drawing is the part's own (a lamp state paints only when a state is set), so each lamp keeps its dark triangle; a light grey triangle of the stencil's size is drawn under it, which leaves a light rim of about 0.25 mm, and the black disc the punched lamp opening drew is covered in the panel's colour. The three lamps by the console and management jacks are arrows too (Figure 1-9, PDF p18, printed 1-16, "Console LEDs": 1 USB console LED, 2 RJ-45 console LED; Table 1-10 gives their colours): they were round dots and are arrow lamps now, down for the USB console LED, right for the RJ-45 console LED (the up skin turned 90 degrees: a lamp, not a connector) and up under the management jack.

A white or silver body for the RJ-45 part. The console jack, the management jack and the 48 jack-block jacks are `std/rj45-ganged@2`, whose only skin paints a near-black body with light grey shoulders. The stencil draws the console and management jacks on a white plate (#efefef, 10086 px of each, boxes (4782,86,4959,226) and (4998,86,5175,226)) round a dark opening, so a plate of that colour and outline (15.6 x 12.34 mm) is drawn under each of the two jacks and the part keeps its own body. On the 48 block jacks the stencil draws charcoal bodies with white shoulders, where the render has near-black bodies with light grey shoulders; left: the part's skin. Request: an `std/rj45` skin with a white body or white shoulders. The latch stays up and the contacts down, as the stencil shows them.

A USB-A skin with a silver interior and the tongue at the left, as the stencil shows. `std/usb-a@1` is placed with `skin: usb2` and rotated 90 degrees, and draws a black opening (#17191c) with a pale tongue (#d5d9de) to the right of the middle of the vertical opening; the stencil draws a silver-grey shell with the tongue at the left. Neither skin of the part draws a silver interior (`default` draws a blue tongue, `usb2` a white one, in the same place), so the part stays as it is. The only way to bring the tongue to the left with this skin is a 270 degree turn of the placed part, which is a rotation and is the owner's to decide. Figure 1-1 (PDF p4, printed 1-2) is too small at this port to say more. The shell around the part is drawn silver (#7b7b7b).

A mini-B skin with the five contacts in the lower half of the opening. `std/mini-usb@1` draws the flat edge at the top, bevelled corners at the bottom and the five contacts (#7a8087) in the upper half; the stencil has the same flat edge and bevel and the contacts in the lower half. The stencil is the only source of the contact side: Figure 1-5 (USB Mini-Type B Port, PDF p9, printed 1-7) draws a mini-B port with the bevelled corners at the top and contacts both on its tongue and in a row below it, which does not settle the side for this connector as it is mounted, and Figure 1-1 (PDF p4, printed 1-2) is too small. The part's skin is not edited and the connector is not turned: turning it would put the bevel on top, and a rotation after merge is a major version.

A version of the SFP+ cage part with the stencil's silver frame (#cfcfcf, 1423 px of each cage), its two clips on the right side (#bdbdbd with black edges), its two small squares near the top (#707070), its gold contacts at the lower left and its pull tab inside the opening. The part's own skin paints a grey collar (#9aa0a8) round a dark opening and its skin is not edited here. Drawn outside or under the part's box: the silver as the surround the part leaves visible (about 0.5 mm each side), the black projection at each cage's foot (#000000, 861 px, box (4570,427,4652,441)), the silver pull tab (#c1c5cb, 240 px, box (4588,416,4636,421); all but about 0.2 mm of it lies under the part's box and is hidden) and the white numeral tab under each cage (#f2f2f2, 2112 px, box (4570,450,4652,477)) with its numeral in #595959 (70 px, box (4600,456,4624,474)). Not drawn: the clips, the squares and the gold contacts, because they lie inside the cage's own opening and would paint over the part's skin. Request: `std/sfp` with the clips, squares, contacts and pull tab in its opening.

The "MGMT" and "BASET" legend right of the management jack. The stencil prints it vertically in yellow (#ffff99, 341 px, box (5190,95,5215,212)): the letters M, G, M, T, then a gap, then B, A, S, E, T, one above the other and upright, each 0.78 mm tall, 10.3 mm in all (it reads "BASET", with no hyphen, at 6x). A legend 0.78 mm tall is under the 1.5 mm font size the library's legend test asks for, so it is not drawn. Wanted: a photograph or a dimensioned front that gives the legend at a size that reads.

The photograph shows the three pins of the AC inlet as dark pockets, each with a small light mark. It also shows two curved light lines inside the inlet's foot. The render draws light grey pin blocks. The inlet is std/c14-inlet@1, which many parts place, so a new version of that part draws the pins, not this device. The pin pockets are left as a later part of their own.
the buried marks moved clear of the components that paint over them

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

an `attrs.performance` section; `cpu`, `memory` in a missing `attrs.platform` section; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power`; one of `operating-temp`, `operating-temp-f2b`, `operating-temp-b2f` in a missing `attrs.environmental` section (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 1 bay (rear 1); `physical-context` on port groups rj45, sfp-plus - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

airflow.note: The guide names a fan exhaust on the rear panel, counts no fans and gives no direction; no airflow is set and no fan redundancy is claimed. The exhaust is drawn where Figure 1-10 and the photograph put it.

colour.note: Front: this model's own NetBox front (cisco-ws-c2960s-48lpd-l.front.png, 1080 x 107 px) is a photograph of a Catalyst 2960 Series SI, another product, and is not read. The front takes the colours the four 2960-S stencils agree on: the bezel #255e6d (median of 7000 px, box (700,6,1200,20) of a 5475 x 503 px stencil; the lower edge, box (700,482,1200,497), reads the same), the charcoal panel #404040 (box (435,30,480,110)), the Mode button #255e6d (box (330,435,385,460)) and the console surround #bbd5d8 (box (4800,70,4850,90)); the WS-C2960S-48FPD-L, -48TD-L, -24PD-L and -24TD-L stencils give the same medians in every box. Figure 1-1 (PDF p4, printed 1-2), Cisco's own colour drawing of the 48FPD-L, draws the same scheme (a dark teal front edge round a charcoal panel, yellow frames round the jack blocks) and is the guide's own evidence that the teal is Cisco's finish. So `chassis.color` is #404040 and the teal edge, the console surround and the yellow frames are drawn; every figure is `estimated`, another model's reading. Rear: The rear is drawn in the chassis colour #404040. The only rear in colour with the FlexStack slot is the NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-48LPD-L (cisco-ws-c2960s-48lpd-l.rear.png, 1516 x 150 px), whose plain plate reads #3f4447 (median of 2000 px, box (440,15,520,40)) and whose fitted module's frame reads #3f565d (box (230,137,330,142)); the NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-24TS-L rear (cisco-ws-c2960s-24ts-l.rear.png, 1102 x 97 px, a model with no FlexStack slot, read for colour only) reads #404145 (box (520,8,590,24)). The drawn #404040 is within 7 levels of 255 of each. Figure 1-10 (PDF p19, printed 1-17) draws the rear pale grey (#d4d6d8, box (330,150,430,185) of the converted figure), shaded by the light on each face; the two photographs and the figure disagree, so the photographs' charcoal is kept and the gap `faceplate-colour` says so.

console.note: Figure 1-1 callouts 5 and 6 and "Management Ports" (Figure 1-5, PDF p9): the USB mini-Type B console port and the RJ-45 console port are one console, and the USB port has priority when both are cabled (Table 1-10). The management port is its own (callout 7).

controls-and-lamps.note: The eight switch lamps (SYST, RPS, MSTR, STAT, DPLX, SPED, STCK, PoE) stand in a column at 7.1 mm, pitched 2.53 mm, the Mode button below them (Figure 1-7, PDF p13, printed 1-11: System, RPS, Master, Status, Duplex, Speed, Stack, PoE, Mode button; the PoE lamp is "only on switch models that support PoE", which this one does). Port lamps are the two small arrows above each column pair, up for the upper port and down for the lower; their meaning depends on the selected mode (Table 1-9). The arrows by the console jacks are the USB and RJ-45 console lamps (Table 1-10, PDF p18, printed 1-16); their text is not on the metal.

ears-and-kits.note: Figure 1-12 (PDF p36, printed 1-12) "Attaching Brackets for 19-inch Racks": front-mounting, mid-mounting and rear-mounting positions, with number-8 Phillips flat-head screws (48-0655-01); Figure 1-13 (PDF p37, printed 1-13): number-12 Phillips pan-head screws (48-0523-01) for the rack and a black Phillips machine screw (48-0654-01) for the cable guide. The text says four screws attach each bracket's long side to the switch. The 19-inch brackets are in the box, so they are not a kit. No position is dimensioned, so none carries an `at`. The ETSI bracket is printed "700-19781XX" (PDF p34, printed 1-10), with its revision digits unread: it is a gap and not a kit.

front-console-end.note: The shapes at the console end are read from the NetBox front elevations of the WS-C2960S-48FPD-L, -48TD-L, -24PD-L and -24TD-L (cisco-ws-c2960s-<model>-l.front.png, 5475 x 503 px, 11.345 px per mm, the chassis starting 216 px in, so one pixel is 0.09 mm). The four agree on every shape here. A model whose own stencil is another product is read from them. The legend band's left end slopes from (384.2, 2.1) to (394.5, 4.6) mm: the first teal pixel of each row runs from 4584 to 4683 px over rows 26 to 50. The dark panel's top-right corner is rounded at about 2.2 mm: the teal ends at 5191 px in row 53 and at 5213 px from row 77. The console surround stops at 24.42 mm under the mini-B jack and at 21.24 mm under the RJ-45 jack, with the step at 402.1 mm, so the surround and its dark panel are two rectangles each, and the port lamp below stands on the panel. The stencil rounds the inside of the step by about 0.9 mm and it is drawn square here. The mini-B's lower corners show the surround's teal in the stencil, so two teal triangles, 0.8 by 1.2 mm, cover the hole's black beside the part's bevels.

front-plates.note: The ring, channel, silver plate and bar round each block of jacks, the yellow number tags above them and the yellow tick band under them, the console and management jack plates, the USB shell, the SFP+ frames with their pull tabs and numeral tabs, the Mode button's rim, the arrow fills and the USB symbol are placed as the WS-C2960S-48FPD-L stencil gives them (cisco-ws-c2960s-48fpd-l.front.png, 11.345 px per mm, the chassis starting 216 px in), which the 48LPD-L stencil matches in layout and in every colour sampled above. The stencil is a community artist's flat render and these are that artist's palette; no photograph from Cisco of the front is held. The yellow outline stays round the white ring because the figure is isometric and too small to tell a ring from a frame.

gate-1-front.note: No held document draws this model's front. It has the same 48 PoE+ ports and two SFP+ slots as the 48FPD-L, so every position is carried from cisco/ws-c2960s-48fpd, which was read from the NetBox front elevation of the WS-C2960S-48FPD-L at 11.345 px per mm (5475 x 503 px, aspect 10.88 against 10.86 for the 19-inch ear-to-ear width). The 48 jacks agree with Table 1-1 (four blocks of twelve in two rows), and the USB Type A, mini-B, RJ-45 console, management and two SFP+ slots agree with Figure 1-1 callouts 3 to 7. Every position is `estimated`: it is another model's reading, used because this model's own documents name the same parts.

inlet.note: The inlet is an IEC C14 appliance inlet, read from Figures 1-10 and 1-11 (a three-pin keyed inlet with a rating label beside it) and the NetBox WS-C2960S-48LPD-L rear photograph, which shows it. The guide does not name the connector type; it says "Use the supplied AC power cord" and describes an optional power cord retainer (PWR-CLP=, PDF p42, printed 1-18). Position is read from that photograph (3.41 px per mm from the 444.5 mm width, 1516 px).

jacks.note: Row 1 starts 11.72 mm down the face and row 2 at 26.71, 15.0 apart; the first block's first jack at 24.06 mm from the chassis side and the blocks 89.4 mm apart (6 x 13.97 plus a 5.58 gutter), as on the 48FPD-L. Upper-row jacks take the 180-degree rotation the 4948E's upper row takes.

legend.note: The legend "Catalyst 2960-S Series PoE+ 10G" is the NetBox stencil's text on the WS-C2960S-48FPD-L and the WS-C2960S-24PD-L, both PoE+ models with two SFP+ slots. Figure 1-1 shows only "2960-S" under the console callout. It is carried for this model from those two stencils, which are community art, not this model's own document.

lifecycle.note: No lifecycle date is carried. The end-of-sale notices are not held; only titles and list dates would be, and this model's is not among them.

numbering.note: Ports run left to right from the far left, port 1 above port 2 in each pair, and the module slots are 49 and 50 (the note under Figure 1-3, PDF p5, printed 1-3). The numerals are carried on the face as printed on the strip above the jacks. Interface names are in the community NetBox device type only: GigabitEthernet1/0/1 to 1/0/48, TenGigabitEthernet1/0/1 and 1/0/2 for the two slots and FastEthernet0 for the management port.

power.note: Spec Table 1-2, row Catalyst 2960S-48LPD-L: AC input 100 to 240 VAC autoranging, 5 to 2 A, 50 to 60 Hz; DC input for the RPS 2300 +12 V @4 A and -52 V @8 A; power consumption 100 W, 341 BTUs per hour (footnote 1: the power consumed internally by the switch at 120 VAC, 60 Hz); power rating 0.48 KVA. The PoE budget is 370 W (Table 1-1; "PoE+", 30 W per port maximum, 370-W switch maximum, spec Table 1-2). The supply is built in: "The switch is powered through the internal power supply" (AC Power Connector, PDF p21-22, printed 1-19 to 1-20), so it is part of the chassis and not a bay.

rear.note: The rear is the stacking models' common rear (Figure 1-10, with the RPS connector: callouts 1 FlexStack module slot and cover, 2 fan exhaust, 3 RPS connector, 4 AC power connector). Positions come from the NetBox 48LPD-L rear photograph (3.41 px per mm along its width), which is this model's own rear by its model name but whose printed ratings match none of the five rows of spec Tables 1-2 and 1-3. It shows a C2960S-STACK module fitted; this device shows the blank cover (the module is optional: "FlexStack Ports", PDF p21, printed 1-19) and takes the module as a configuration. Spec Table 1-2 lists a DC input for the RPS 2300 for this model, so the RPS connector is present. The guide says "If you are not using an RPS with your switch, use the two Phillips pan-head screws to attach the RPS connector cover" (Figure 1-15, PDF p39, printed 1-15), so the connector is drawn open, as the photograph shows it. It is the part cisco/rps2300-connector@2 (interface `cisco-rps2300`), seated at the plate's place; the rating strip stays chassis art. Measured on the photograph at 3.41 px per mm: a metal plate 72.8 x 22.6 mm at (285.0, 21.4) with a raised rating strip above it (49.2 x 3.8 mm at 297.7, 17.9), a black shroud 48.2 x 11.3 mm at (298.4, 24.0) holding a cream housing 46.9 x 9.7 mm, and in it two rows of eleven cavities on a 4.17 mm pitch, with a screw hole at each end of the plate. Eleven across is what the serial-number figures draw (PDF p55-56, printed 1-5 to 1-6); Figure 1-10 draws seven in a smaller figure, and the photograph and the larger figures are followed. The warning label above the plate ("DC inputs for remote power supply specified in manual", with a triangle) is printed on the metal. It sits at (294.0, 5.9), 45.2 x 9.7 mm, and is drawn as the photograph prints it. The rating strip over the pins and the rating plate beside the inlet (32.7 x 13.4 mm at (351.0, 6.1)) are drawn blank. The printed legends are left to a later touch of their own (see the gaps `rear-label-text` and `rps-connector-part`). The inlet sits in a moulded black surround 29.3 x 22.5 mm at (387.6, 8.3). The fan exhaust is a honeycomb of hexagons about 9.7 x 8.5 mm on an 8.8 mm column pitch (21 cells, flat-topped), drawn with the library's `vent` pattern scaled by 2.0 with `pattern-pitch` to that pitch over a plate in the web's colour (the photograph's web reads #404345, box (540,44,705,140), the holes #040507), with the two light cut edges above and below the field (#b9bcba, box (533,40,712,46)). Four pan-head screws, 6.8 mm across, stand at 7.3, 111.4, 274.2 and 436.4 mm along and 28.7 mm down; the first is on the module's flange and is drawn with the cover. The FlexStack slot is the fitted module's stepped frame (see the blank cover's contract). The stamped corner marks round the fan and the small drilled hole are drawn (see `rear-details`).

rear-details.note: Read off the NetBox rear photograph of the WS-C2960S-48LPD-L (1516 x 150 px; 3.41 px per mm from the 444.5 mm width). Each figure is the pixel points read at 4 times on a gridded crop, rounded to 0.1 mm and good to about 0.3 mm. Drawn: the lid's lit edge along the top (rows 0 to 3, mean #95979a) and the light rim round the inlet surround. Also drawn: the two oval tabs above and below the inlet (stroke #5c6062, fill #323637). Also drawn: the round hole left of the fan (rim #838788, 125 px; dark #171717). Also drawn: the twelve stamped bracket marks (two groups of six). Also drawn: the chassis' diagonal edge at the far right (line #5c6061) and the steps under it. The 24TS-L photograph, a model with no FlexStack slot, shows the same lit top edge. The stamped marks are under 2 px wide, so the sampled extremes (dark #232729 over 353 px, lit #959c9e over 1084 px) overstate their contrast. The drawn ink is each extreme blended 40 percent into the plate's #3f4447, which is #34383b dark and #61676a lit. The photograph is another model's rear, so the same marks are carried to this one. The printed legends and marks are not drawn here: each is left to a later touch of its own.

side-left.note: The left wall's 29 openings (17 peanut slots, 7 round holes, 5 small rectangles) are placed from photographs of the product. The photographs show two 299 mm models, a 24-port and a 48-port. Each opening is placed in millimetres from the rear and top edges, good to about 4 mm along and 2 mm across. The two photographs differ by at most 3.5 mm along the wall and 1.3 mm across it. Figure 1-10 (PDF p19, printed 1-17) gives the pattern: the count and kind of each opening. Figure 1-10 is captioned "Catalyst 2960-S Switch Rear Panel with Stacking Module Slot and RPS connector". It is a perspective view, so it gives the pattern but not the positions along the wall. The scale along the wall comes from each photographed model's own length, 299 mm (Table 1-3, PDF p65). This model is 386 mm deep (Table 1-2, PDF p63). The scale across the wall comes from the printed 44.45 mm height. Sizes along the wall come from the photographs too. In the figure, the rear group's slots and bars read about 1.4 times too long along the wall. No photograph of a 386 mm model's wall is held. Assumed: each group keeps its distance from its own end, leaving a plain stretch 87 mm longer than on the 299 mm models. Its four callouts do not name the openings: the figure shows 29 openings; the guide does not say what they are for. They stay drawn as marks. The openings' colour, #141414, is a stand-in dark; the figure's grey is shading. The wall keeps the device's colour. Figure 1-10 shows each of the 17 slots with a waist. The drawn outlines have none; the waists are a later part of their own.

sources.note: Catalyst 2960-S Switch Hardware Installation Guide, OL-19732-04, 82 pages (the PDF prints its number and no date; Cisco URL https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/switches/lan/catalyst2960/hardware/installation/guide_stack/2960SHIG.pdf). Pages below are PDF pages with the printed page after them. Table 1-1 (PDF p3-4, printed 1-1 to 1-2) lists the model; the appendix's Table 1-2 (PDF p62-63) gives this model's row; Figure 1-10 "Catalyst 2960-S Switch Rear Panel with Stacking Module Slot and RPS connector" (PDF p19, printed 1-17) is the rear of the stacking models. The guide draws no front of this model: Figure 1-1 "Catalyst 2960S-48FPD-L Front Panel" (PDF p4, printed 1-2) is a sibling's, and the guide says "All the 24- and 48-port switches have similar components" (Front Panel, PDF p4). Community NetBox (second opinion only, not Cisco's): the WS-C2960S-48LPD-L device type and its rear elevation, a photograph of this model's rear. Its front elevation is not used: it is a photograph of a "Catalyst 2960 Series SI", a different product with no USB port. No data sheet, no vendor 3D model and no photograph of this model's front is held. The pages were read through the PDF's text layer and the converted figures were viewed.
